Independently re-derived. Case 1: a segment of length 60 mm parallel to the axis at constant 40 mm, revolved through pi/2, gives A = (pi/2)(40)(60) = 1200 pi = 3769.91 mm^2. Verified by an independent elementary route that does not reuse the theorem: the swept surface is a quarter of a cylindrical lateral surface of radius 40 and height 60, whose full area is 2 pi (40)(60) = 4800 pi, one quarter of which is 1200 pi — an exact match. Case 2 carries the discrimination: the hypotenuse of a 30-40-50 right triangle placed with vertices at (30, 0), (60, 0) and (30, 40), revolved about x = 0. Both centroid distances were re-derived from those vertices: hypotenuse length sqrt(900 + 1600) = 50 mm, curve centroid at the midpoint (45, 20) giving r_bar_c = 45 mm, and the centroid of the triangular AREA at the vertex average (40, 13.33) giving 40 mm. A = (pi/2)(45)(50) = 1125 pi = 3534.29 mm^2 from the curve centroid, against 1000 pi = 3141.59 mm^2 from the area centroid — a gap of 125 pi, about 11 percent, making the line-centroid versus area-centroid distinction visible numerically rather than asserted in prose.
